newsitem.title: UK: Argentina mandates HSBC and UBS for 10-yr stg bond.
newsitem.headline: Argentina mandates HSBC and UBS for 10-yr stg bond.

text.p: Argentina has mandated HSBC and UBS for an expected 10-year sterling bond, joint lead manager UBS said on Thursday.
The bond is likely to be for up to 200 million stg, bankers said.
"The bond is expected to have a 10-year maturity of around 200 million stg," a UBS syndicate official said. But he said pricing of the deal was too early to discuss.
"We're excited about the bond and it is clearly an appealing maturity and we will launch the transaction towards the end of next week after investor presentations," he added.
A syndicate manager away from the joint lead managers said a 10-year deal for Argentina could be priced to yield 280 basis points over gilts.
"A level around 270-280 b.p. is possible," a dealer said.
Another syndicate offical said a range of 250-260 b.p. was also mooted.
"At the wider end of a 250-260 range," he added.
On Monday Argentina's Finance Secretary Pablo Guidotti said the country was going to issue a 10-year bond denominated in sterling.
Argentina has only once tapped the sterling sector with a 100 million stg five-year bond via SBC Warburg in July last year.
It was lauched to yield 390 basis points over gilts and has tightened to trade at around 211 b.p. over, dealers said on Thursday.
The paper pays a coupon of 11.50 percent. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
